title: Chemically Interpretable Graph Neural Networks Reveal Structure–Property Relationships in Acrylate‐Based UV Coatings
content:
Machine learning applications allow the interpretation of molecule structure and its influence on target properties. Such techniques have been applied for the analysis of an UV coating system revealing the structure-property relations of (meth)acrylate reactive diluents.


ABSTRACT

Understanding how monomer structure relates to the properties of crosslinked coatings requires both predictive modeling and chemically informed interpretation. Here, the attention-based graph neural network AttentiveFP was applied to an experimental data set of UV coatings prepared by varying monomer structure while maintaining the remaining formulation components and preparation conditions. AttentiveFP was selected for its integration of molecular graph learning and atom-level attention visualization, supporting the focus of this research on property-specific prediction assessment and chemical interpretation. Molecular graphs were used to predict thermal, mechanical, network-related, and surface properties. Ten-fold cross-validation yielded coefficients of determination above 0.8 for glass transition temperature, Young's modulus, and storage modulus, whereas gloss was less predictable. Attention analysis revealed property-dependent patterns: polymerizable groups received prominent attention in glass transition temperature predictions, while pendant group architecture was emphasized for storage modulus and pendulum hardness. These patterns were consistent with chemical considerations involving network connectivity, segmental mobility, and local rigidity, providing hypotheses for further investigation rather than quantitative physical contributions. These results demonstrate that experimentally grounded graph-based learning provides not only accurate property prediction but also interpretable mechanistic insight into polymer structure–property relationships, establishing a framework for data-driven and chemically interpretable material design.
